intent: Compare the change in median executive pay at the largest US companies with the change in typical worker pay from 1970 to 2000.

requirements.question: Are all required line series shown in every declared panel?
Does the visualization show the change in median executive pay at the largest US companies from 1970 to 2000?

units.claim: All 1 required series appear in panel single chart.
accept: every required series is visible and correctly labeled in this panel
reject: series assigned to the wrong panel

units.claim: Median CEO pay at the largest US companies increased from $0.85 in 1970 to $5.30 in 2000.
units.computation: last_value - first_value = 5.30 - 0.85 = 4.45 USD; ratio = 5.30 / 0.85 ≈ 6.24; percentage change ≈ 523.5%
accept: CEO pay rose from $0.85 in 1970 to $5.30 in 2000
an increase of about $4.45 (roughly 6.2x, or about 524%)
reject: CEO pay was flat from 1970 to 2000
only one endpoint is shown without the other

optional_valid: Mentioning the intermediate CEO pay values in 1980 ($1.30) and 1990 ($2.30) as supporting detail for the upward trend.
Comparing median CEO pay change with typical worker pay change is optional_valid for V1 because the worker-pay series is absent from data_table.csv; it must not count as a required unit.
unsupported_to_avoid: Any specific typical worker pay values or percentage changes, because the supplied table summary contains only the CEO pay series.
Causal explanations for the pay gap, such as stock options, globalization, or union decline, since the table provides no evidence for causes.
Claims about years outside 1970–2000 or about companies other than the largest US companies.
The V1 data_table.csv contains only one unlabeled pay series and no typical-worker-pay series, so the CEO-versus-worker change is not encoded as a required G1 unit.
review_notes: The supplied table summary contains only the CEO pay series; the typical worker pay series needed for the comparison in U2 is absent, so U2 is marked needs_review.
U1 uses the 1970 and 2000 rows explicitly present in the table summary; the row with empty x and point_order 1 (value 0.822) is not used as an endpoint because it lacks an explicit year.
The chart structure reports panel_count 1 with an empty panel label, so all units apply to the single panel.
